questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Sulphanilic acid gives esterification test for carboxyl group.

Statement II: Sulphanilic acid gives red colour in Lassigne’s test for extra element detection.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Sulphanilic acid is p-amino benzene sulphonic acid. It has no –COOH group hence no esterification test for carboxyl group. 

But it has sulphur, and nitrogen atom hence gives red colour in Lassigne's test for extra element detection.

Hence, statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.

questions.q: An organic compound is estimated through Dumas method and was found to evolve 6 moles of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}, 4$ moles of $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}$ and 1 mole of nitrogen gas. The formula of the compound is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$\left[\mathrm{C}_{x} \mathrm{H}_{y} \mathrm{~N}_{z}\right] \frac{\text { Dumas }}{\text { method }} \rightarrow 6 \mathrm{CO}_{2}+4 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{N}_{2}$

Mol of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}=6,$ so $\mathrm{mol}$ of $\mathrm{C}$ is $=6$ 

Mol of $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}=4$, so $\mathrm{mol}$ of $\mathrm{H}$ is $=8$ 

Mol of $\mathrm{N}_{2}=1,$ so $\mathrm{mol}$ of $\mathrm{N}$ is $=2\therefore$ Formula is $\mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{8} \mathrm{~N}_{2}$

questions.q: Lassaigne's test is used for detection of:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Lassaigne's test helps to detect Nitrogen, Sulphur, and Halogens in organic compounds. Here, sodium metal Na is heated in the presence of the organic compound inside a fusion tube. The primary objective of this test is that all the available elements are converted by Sodium metal Na into the ionic state. Lassaigne test reaction for sodium is given below:

N+Na+C→NaCN

S+2Na→Na2S

X+Na→NaX

In the third experiment, X can be anything such as Cl, Br or I.
